format.note: Fields are present and concrete, and observability labels distinguish static observation from judgment. However, given/when do not express the TypeScript/source activation restrictions, and when requires persistence although the specified trigger also covers read-only subset requests. The finding fact names only growing call counts, not growing records touched.

generality.note: The query and changed-record persistence guidance generalizes across stores and business domains; examples use ordinary, neutral record concepts.

decisionUseful.note: Implementation guidance is concrete, but read-only handlers are excluded by the wording of when. The blanket loop prohibition in evidence and verifier_detail also conflicts with the permitted update-by-id approach when several changed records need individual writes.

missing: Activation for subset reads that do not persist changes: the spec covers any handler/use case needing the subset, whereas when requires both reading and persisting.
extraObligations: Evidence requires 'no store call inside a loop' and verifier_detail flags all awaited store/adapter calls in loops. The spec prohibits per-record read N+1, not individually updating the bounded set of modified records.

The verifier threshold 'records touched <= records used plus a small constant' imposes an additive bound not specified by the spec; bounded work proportional to records actually used can include multiple touches per used record.

requiredFixes: Change when to cover reading the needed subset, with changed-record persistence conditional on changes being made.
Align activation facts with the stated given/when scope, documenting any intended language/file restrictions, and represent history-dependent records touched as well as call counts.
Restrict the loop checks to per-record reads/N+1 fetching; permit per-id writes to only the modified records when their cost is bounded by records actually used.
Replace the additive records-touched threshold with a bound proportional to records actually used and independent of history size.
summary: The convention captures the main indexed-subset and changed-record-only obligation without application-specific leakage. It needs broader activation for read-only requests and narrower verification criteria so legitimate bounded writes and proportional record access are not rejected.
